title: Ôn luyện Từ vựng thi vào 10 số 25: Natural disasters (Set 1)

lessons.title: nhúng từ
lessons.contentHtml:
Hãy cùng học các từ vựng thuộc chủ điểm Natural disasters (Set 1) ngay nhé!


Nhấn ᐸ / ᐳ để chuyển sang từ khác và 🔊 để nghe phát âm.

Bạn nên đọc kĩ nghĩa, ví dụ và nghe phát âm của tất cả các từ vựng trước khi nhấn "Next" để chuyển sang luyện tập ở mức nhận biết.

vocabTable.example: The rescue team helped the villagers _____ in a nearby field after the earthquake.

vocabTable.meaning: từ vựng chủ điểm Natural disasters (Set 1)
vocabTable.example: Complete the text, using the words given. Natural disasters can happen in different types of weather. In 14.1 areas, storms often bring heavy rain and strong winds. These storms can 14.2 floods, which damage homes and roads. In colder places, a 14.3 winter can lead to problems like blocked roads and frozen pipes. People need to stay warm and safe when the temperature drops below zero on the 14.4 scale. Sometimes, disasters like earthquakes or hurricanes can completely 14.5 buildings and leave people without homes. It is important to prepare for natural disasters by having food, water, and a plan. Staying informed about the weather and listening to warnings can also help keep everyone safe. Natural disasters are dangerous, but being ready can reduce their impact.

vocabTable.meaning: từ vựng chủ điểm Natural disasters (Set 1)
vocabTable.example: Complete the conversation, using the following words. Liam: Hi, Sarah. The weather today is 35 degrees 12.1 ! It feels so hot. Sarah: Yes, and they said heavy 12.2 is coming later in the evening. Liam: Really? The water will cover the streets. Sarah: That's right. And if it doesn’t stop, there might be a 12.3 . Liam: That's too bad! They also mentioned a 12.4 might form if the wind gets stronger. Sarah: That’s scary! We should stay inside and prepare for the worst. Liam: Good idea, Sarah. Let’s check the news again before it gets dark.

vocabTable.example: Read the conversation and then choose the correct answer to fill in each blank. Emily: Hi, John. Did you hear about the 13.1 tidal tropical storm on the news? John: Yes, they said it might cause strong 13.2 winds snows tomorrow. Emily: That’s scary. And it often brings too much rain, which turns the ground into 13.3 mud soil . John: You’re right. It’s hard to move when everything is wet and slippery. Emily: I hope the warning 13.4 system canal works well to keep people safe this time. John: Me too. It helps everyone prepare before the storm arrives. Emily: We should stay inside and be ready for anything. John: Good idea, Emily. Let’s also check the weather updates later tonight.
